TASK ID: independent-set-to-vertex-cover

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Independent Set to Vertex Cover. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Independent Set and TARGET is Vertex Cover. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = IndependentSet
Independent Set.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has an independent set of AT LEAST k vertices: k
vertices with no edge between any two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k > n is always no. With no edges,
every set of vertices is independent.

TARGET = VertexCover
Vertex Cover.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a vertex cover of AT MOST k vertices: a set of
vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
every edge.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-5zv901co
All input files are in this directory; run every command from it and write your files here. problems.py is long (about 500 lines): you do not need to read it to know the formats, which are given above. It provides SOURCE and TARGET with is_yes(instance), validate(instance) and random_instance(rng, scale); search it (e.g. with grep) only if you need something specific.

REQUIRED OUTPUT: create reduce.py in the workspace, defining
    reduce(instance) -> instance

The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

{"command":"cd /tmp/reduction-5zv901co && cat <<'EOF' > reduce.py
"""Polynomial-time reduction from Independent Set to Vertex Cover.

For a graph G = (V, E), a set S is an independent set if and only if its
complement V \ S is a vertex cover.  Indeed, S has no edge inside it iff
every edge has at least one endpoint outside S, i.e. in V \ S.

Therefore G has an independent set of size at least k iff G has a vertex
cover of size at most n - k.  The reduction keeps the same graph and maps
k to n - k.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    n = instance["n"]
    edges = [[u, v] for u, v in instance["edges"]]
    k = instance["k"]
    return {"n": n, "edges": edges, "k": n - k}
EOF
echo written && ls -la"}
